turns.t: Hi, doctor. Thanks for fitting me in. I've got a pain in my left Achilles tendon, and it's been bugging me.
Tell me about it. Where exactly?
About two inches above the heel, at the back. It's sore when I go for a run, especially the first few minutes.
Does it ease once you warm up? ~
Yes, it eases, then it comes back after I've stopped and cooled down. ~
How about first thing in the morning, when you get out of bed? ~
Stiff and sore for the first few steps. Then it's okay. ~
Did you feel a pop or a sudden snap at any point?
No pop. Nothing sudden. It built up slowly.
How long has it been building up?
About six weeks, I'd say.
Okay. Let me have a look at it. Take off your shoe and sock, and stand facing the wall.
Sure. ~
Now rise up onto your toes, both feet, slowly. ~
Okay. That's fine. A bit sore on the left. ~
There's tenderness about two inches above the heel, right over the tendon.
Yes, that's the spot. ~
And the tendon feels thickened there, compared with the right one.
Is that bad? ~
Any problem with the other leg, or any numbness, anything like that?
No, nothing like that. It's only that heel.
Let me explain what I think is going on. The tendon has been overloaded and has become irritated and thickened. I think this looks like Achilles tendinopathy.
Is it torn? ~
There was no pop and you can rise onto your toes, so a full tear is very unlikely. ~
That's a relief. ~
I'd like to start naproxen, 250 mg, twice a day with food, for one week.
Okay. And can I keep running? ~
I'd cut your running by half and avoid hills and speed work for now.
That's going to be hard. ~
I'd also like to arrange an ultrasound of the Achilles tendon, and I'll refer you to physiotherapy for a loading programme.
When will that be? ~
The ultrasound within two weeks, and physiotherapy will call you. ~
Great, thank you. ~
Do the calf stretches that the physio shows you, and avoid stretching the tendon hard until then.
I'll be careful. ~
Any other questions? ~
No, I think that covers it. ~
Good. Take care. ~
Thanks, doctor. ~
